subject: Finlytics POC - success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan@finlytics.com>, Aisha Banerjee <aisha@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T17:15:00Z
Subject: Finlytics POC - success criteria & next steps

Thanks again for the call today — great conversation. Below is a short recap plus a proposed POC plan so we can sync on success criteria and owners.

Recap (discovery highlights)
- Primary goal: validate Redwood improves query latency for Finlytics' analytics assistants and reduces per-token cost by >= 30% vs current setup.
- Data: ~500k anonymized transaction records + metadata; test queries will be a mix of short conversational prompts and long analytical queries (~1.5k token average).
- Security: customer wants VPC/private option; SOC2 and access audit logs are required.

Proposed POC (high-level)
1) Kickoff & access (week 0) — share test dataset + grant read-only S3 access; agree on redaction approach.
2) Baseline run (week 1) — run 1k representative queries against current infra (you provide query set).
3) Redwood integration & tuning (week 2) — deploy model variant, configure batching/caching, quantization profile.
4) Eval & metrics (week 3) — measure p95 latency, throughput, cost/token, and qualitative quality checks on 100 flagged prompts.
5) Wrap & next steps (week 4) — review results and discuss Dedicated/Private options.

Success criteria (please confirm / modify)
- p95 inference latency <= 250ms for short prompts, <= 800ms for long analytical prompts.
- Cost reduction >= 30% per token compared to baseline.
- No data exfiltration concerns; audit logs enabled for all requests.

Owners / asks
- Finlytics: provide query set (representative sample) and temporary access to sanitized dataset (Jordan / Aisha).
- Redwood: Marissa (program lead) and Marcus (solutions engineer) to provision environment, run baseline, and share dashboards.

Attachments: Finlytics-POC-plan-v1.xlsx (POC timeline & milestone tracker) — attached.

Next steps
- Jordan / Aisha: confirm success criteria and availability for kickoff week of Oct 18.
- If agreed, we'll book a 30–45 min kickoff and share the Drive folder + initial checklist.

Thanks — Marissa

Date: 2026-10-06T09:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Finlytics POC - success criteria & next steps

Thanks Marissa — really helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

Success criteria we care most about (ranked):
1) End-user latency for analyst chat flows (p95) — target <= 300ms; acceptable <= 450ms.
2) Cost reduction — we want to see >= 25% to justify switching (30% is ideal).
3) Stability & auditability — SOC2 controls + request logs.

Timeline: kickoff week of Oct 18 works on our side. We can provide the query set by Oct 12 EOD.

Questions:
- For the dataset, we’ll share a sanitized S3 bucket. Can Redwood accept temporary IAM role access?
- Do you need an on-prem runner for any parts of the POC?

I attached our internal requirements doc. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

— Jordan
Jordan Park
Head of Platform, Finlytics
jordan@finlytics.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan@finlytics.com>, Aisha Banerjee <aisha@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T15:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Finlytics POC - success criteria & next steps

Appreciate the quick reply and the priorities, Jordan. Answers inline below and a slightly more detailed evaluation plan attached.

- IAM access: Yes — temporary IAM role with read-only S3 permissions works. We'll also provide a short checklist for redaction so we validate anonymization before ingest.
- On-prem runner: not required for the first-phase POC; Redwood hosted + VPC peering should cover your needs. If later you require on-prem, we can scope it as part of Private deployment.

Evaluation plan (milestones & owners)
- Week 0 (Oct 18) Kickoff — agree owners, confirm IAM role access (Finlytics: Jordan), share query set (Finlytics), Redwood set up test environment (Marissa / Marcus).
- Week 1 Baseline — Finlytics run queries against current infra (Jordan) & share results; Redwood runs same queries against test environment (Marcus).
- Week 2 Tuning — Marcus will iterate on batching, caching, and model variant selection; share interim dashboard.
- Week 3 Final eval — compare p95, cost/token, and qualitative quality checks; produce final report.

Deliverables & owners
- Query set + sanitized S3 access: Jordan/Aisha (Finlytics)
- Test environment + dashboard: Marcus (Redwood)
- Final evaluation report: Marissa + Marcus (Redwood)

I also created a shared Drive folder and added the POC milestone tracker (link below). I attached the updated POC plan.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-Finlytics-POC

If that looks good, I'll book the kickoff for Oct 18 and send a calendar invite.

Best — Marissa

Hi Jordan / Aisha — quick nudge as we get close to next week. Short checklist before kickoff: 

- Confirm sanitized S3 access + temp IAM role (Jordan) — requested by Oct 14 EOD.
- Share the query set (Jordan) — requested by Oct 14 EOD so Marcus can run baseline on Mon/Tue.
- Confirm 30–45 min kickoff time slot Oct 18–20. I’ve proposed three slots in the calendar invite (please accept one).

If we don’t get access by Oct 14, we’ll likely need to push the baseline to the following week, which would delay the wrap by ~1 week. If you prefer, we can run a constrained baseline on a smaller query set that doesn't require full dataset access — happy to discuss tradeoffs.

Checklist & links:
- POC milestone tracker: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-Finlytics-POC

Marissa
